name: Nurseries, horticulture and landscaping supply
shape_facts: Business mix: retail nursery, wholesale growing, landscaping projects, garden maintenance contracts, supply of pots, soil and fittings
Number of sites or outlets and growing area
Own-grown plants versus bought-in or imported stock
Customer types: households, housing societies, developers, government or municipal tenders, hotels, corporate offices
Number of malis, landscapers and project crews
Sales channels: walk-in, Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp, Daraz or other marketplaces, delivery apps
Systems: registers, POS, Excel, project spreadsheets
scope_rule: pi notes business and operational problems: plant stock and losses, pricing, sales channels, orders and delivery, project quotes and progress, maintenance contract scheduling, crew attendance, supplier and import issues, collections from developers and clients, and visibility for the owner. pi does not advise on plant care, watering, fertiliser or pesticide choice or doses, pest or disease treatment, plant import permits or quarantine rules, irrigation engineering, or contract law. It records customer and staff roles only, never names, addresses or phone numbers.

vocabulary.paneeri: seedlings or saplings raised for transplanting
vocabulary.sod / grass roll: pre-grown turf laid as a lawn
vocabulary.softscape / hardscape: planting work / paving, stones and structures
vocabulary.BOQ: bill of quantities used in landscaping quotes
vocabulary.retention: part of a project payment held back until handover

problems.phrase: Plants die in the nursery and I only find out at stock count
I don’t know how many of each plant I have across both sites
Popular indoor plants sell out every spring and I reorder late
Staff sell plants at different prices to different people
Cash sales at the counter don’t match the register
Instagram and WhatsApp enquiries pile up and half get no reply
People ask for a price on WhatsApp and never come back
Delivered plants arrive damaged and customers want refunds
Delivery riders take too long and cost too much for small orders
Landscaping quotes take me days to prepare
Projects run over budget and I find out at the end
Developers hold our retention and final payments for months
Maintenance visits get missed and clients complain
Malis’ attendance at client sites can’t be checked
Crews take plants or materials from the site
Imported plants stuck at customs and some die
Supplier sends lower-quality pots than ordered
Water and electricity for the nursery cost more each year
Rent for the nursery land keeps going up
Tender and municipal paperwork takes forever
I can’t tell if retail, projects or maintenance makes the most money
No proper website or online catalogue
Daraz listings show plants we don’t have any more
Customers come once in spring and we never hear from them again
I want to open a second outlet but the first isn’t organised yet
Summer is dead and staff costs stay the same

stock: How do you keep track of plants across your sites?
How do you find out about losses?
pricing and counter: How are prices set and shown to staff?
How is the day’s cash checked?
online enquiries: Where do most enquiries come from now?
projects: How do you prepare a landscaping quote today?
How do you track costs while the job is running?
collections: What’s usually holding the payment up?
maintenance contracts: How do you know a visit actually happened?
crews: How many malis or crew members work on sites?
How do you check attendance and work done?
suppliers and imports: Where do you buy plants and pots from?
business mix: Which part of the business feels most profitable?
growth: What’s the next step you’re thinking about?

seasons: Pakistan: spring (February–April) is the main planting and sales season; monsoon (July–September) is the government and society tree plantation drive period; autumn (October–November) is a second planting season; summer heat (May– June) slows retail and raises plant losses. Housing society handovers and wedding season (November–February) drive landscaping and decor plant demand. UAE: the main landscaping and planting season runs October–April; summer (June–September) is slow with high water and cooling costs and plant stress; Ramadan, Eid, National Day and the winter events season lift corporate and villa orders. Canada: spring rush April–June (Victoria Day weekend is a classic peak), summer maintenance, fall planting and cleanup, and Christmas trees and poinsettias in December; winter is quiet.
care: No advice on plant care, watering, fertiliser, pesticide or herbicide choice or doses, or pest and disease treatment; pi suggests a horticulturist or extension service.
No advice on plant import permits, quarantine or biosecurity rules; pi notes only the delay or paperwork problem.
Heat exhaustion of crews, falls from heights during tree work, chemical exposure, electric shock from irrigation pumps: pi tells them to call emergency services (1122, 999/998, 911) immediately.
Never helps import plants without permits, mislabel species or origin, or bypass tender rules.
Does not record customer names, villa addresses, phone numbers or staff IDs; uses roles and counts.
Tender bribery or “commission” requests: pi declines and moves on.
build_ideas: Plant stock register by species, size and site, with losses logged with photos and reasons
Reorder alerts for fast-selling lines ahead of spring
POS or simple counter app with a fixed price list and daily cash close
WhatsApp and Instagram enquiry inbox with quick-reply catalogue and follow-up reminders
Online catalogue and ordering with delivery slot selection
Delivery tracker with photo proof at drop-off
Landscaping quote builder from a standard rate and item library, producing a branded BOQ
Project cost tracker comparing quoted versus actual materials and labour
Receivables tracker for projects, including retention amounts and release dates
Maintenance contract scheduler with visit check-in, photos and a monthly client report
Business-line profit view: retail, projects, maintenance
Customer list with seasonal reminder messages

exchange.text: We run a nursery and do villa landscaping in Dubai. Maintenance clients keep saying our team didn’t show up.
That’s frustrating, especially if you can’t easily prove otherwise. Noted. How are maintenance visits scheduled at the moment?
The supervisor has a list on paper and calls the guys each morning.
Noted, schedule on paper and calls each morning. When a visit is done, how does anyone know it actually happened?
